Compute the analytic certainty of transition probabilities

Source: R/certainty_lsa.R
certainty_lsa.Rd

certainty_lsa() computes the analytic certainty of every transition probability of a fit from lsa(): how precisely the data pin down each transition probability, and which transitions are estimated precisely enough to be called certain. Under a Dirichlet-Multinomial model the outgoing transitions of each state are a multinomial draw whose probabilities have a Dirichlet posterior, so each transition probability has a Beta posterior with a closed-form mean, standard deviation and credible interval. A transition probability estimated from counts is uncertain in proportion to how often its source state was visited: a probability of 0.5 from 4 departures is far less certain than the same value from 400.

The posterior is computed with a Jeffreys prior by default and needs no resampling. Each transition gets its posterior mean, standard deviation and credible interval, and a posterior tail probability that decides whether it is certain. With inference = "stability" a transition is certain when its posterior stays within a band around the observed probability (by default 75% to 125% of it); with inference = "threshold" it is certain when its posterior lies above a minimum probability. A grouped fit gives one result per group.

The model treats the transitions as independent draws. When sequences differ strongly from one another (for example, a mixture of latent groups with long sequences) it reports more certainty than the data support; use bootstrap_lsa(), which resamples whole sequences, in that case. To compare two groups' transition probabilities with the same model, use bayes_compare_lsa().

Usage

certainty_lsa(
  fit,
  prior = 0.5,
  level_alpha = 0.95,
  inference = c("stability", "threshold"),
  consistency_range = c(0.75, 1.25),
  edge_threshold = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_certainty'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_certainty_group'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_certainty_group'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

fit

An lsa fit from lsa(), or a grouped fit from lsa(..., group = ).

prior

Dirichlet concentration added to every cell. Default 0.5 (the Jeffreys prior).

level_alpha

Credible-interval level. Default 0.95. The certainty decision uses 1 - level_alpha as its threshold.

inference

"stability" (default): a transition is certain when little posterior mass lies outside consistency_range times its observed probability. "threshold": certain when little posterior mass lies below edge_threshold.

consistency_range

Two multipliers of the observed probability that bound the band for inference = "stability". Default c(0.75, 1.25).

edge_threshold

Minimum probability for inference = "threshold". Default NULL, the 10% quantile of the non-zero transition probabilities.

x

An lsa_certainty or lsa_certainty_group object, for the print() and as.data.frame() methods.

...

Not used.

row.names, optional

Not used; present for consistency with the generic.

Value

An object of class c("lsa_certainty", "lsa_bootstrap", "list"). Read it with transitions(), which returns a data frame with one row per transition (from -> to pair) and the columns from, to, observed (count), prob_observed, prob_mean (posterior mean), prob_se (posterior standard deviation), prob_ci_low, prob_ci_high (credible interval), p_value (posterior mass outside the band, or below the threshold), stable (certain), and adj_res_observed, adj_res_stable (the fit's adjusted residual and a copy of stable, used by plot_forest()). Transitions that cannot be estimated (a source state never left, or a structural zero) are NA and never certain. transitions(x, significant = TRUE) keeps the certain transitions.

For a grouped fit, an object of class lsa_certainty_group, a list with one lsa_certainty per group; as.data.frame() stacks their tables with a leading group column. print() shows the settings and the number of certain transitions and returns x invisibly.

References

Johnston, L., & Jendoubi, T. (2026). How delivery mode reshapes resource engagement: A Bayesian differential network analysis. TNA Workshop 2026.

See also

transitions() to read the result; plot.lsa_certainty() and plot_forest() to draw it; bootstrap_lsa() for resampling intervals; bayes_compare_lsa() to compare groups under the same model.

Examples

fit <- lsa(engagement)
cert <- certainty_lsa(fit)
cert
#> <lsa_certainty>  (analytic Dirichlet-Multinomial)
#>   engine:        classical
#>   prior:         Dirichlet(0.50)
#>   CI level:      95%  |  inference: stability
#>   certain edges: 7 of 9
transitions(cert, significant = TRUE)
#>         from         to observed prob_observed prob_mean    prob_se prob_ci_low

#> 2    Average     Active      153     0.2037284 0.2039867 0.01467978   0.1759752

#> 7 Disengaged Disengaged      157     0.4830769 0.4823890 0.02761180   0.4284082
#>   prob_ci_high      p_value stable adj_res_observed adj_res_stable
#> 1    0.7312156 5.560385e-20   TRUE       21.6628107           TRUE
#> 2    0.2334883 6.063196e-04   TRUE      -12.9060384           TRUE

# One table per group
g <- lsa(group_regulation_long, actor = "Actor", action = "Action",
         time = "Time", group = "Achiever")
gcert <- certainty_lsa(g)
gcert
#> <lsa_certainty_group>
#>   groups: 2 (High, Low)
